# $crav1-build-tasks

lane: build | group: Build | starter: no | stage: stable | since: 1.0.0 | prompts: 4
purpose: Build tasks from tasks.md, always in an isolated worker per task; asks which tasks (one, a range, or all).
use_when: You want to build one task, a range, or all unticked tasks
reads: Inside each worker: Reads one `T#` in `tasks.md`, plus `plan.md` and `spec.md`. One task: Reads one `T#` and the persist rule. A range or all: Reads the `T#` queue on one spec.
writes: Inside each worker: Writes the code and the checks that row names, and marks the row `[x]` only when that verify passes. A tick-only row is marked `[x]` by `scripts/tick_only.py` with no worker and no code change. One task: Writes the commit-style rule when it is missing. A range or all: Writes the commit-style rule once when it is missing. When the picked branch is not the build map's name, writes `(map: <picked>)` on that task in the specs repo and does not commit it.
leaves alone: Inside each worker: Leaves `spec.md` and other tasks alone. One task: Leaves product code, `spec.md`, push, and the pull request alone in this chat. A range or all: Leaves product code, commits, `spec.md`, push, and the pull request alone in this chat.
limits: Inside each worker: stops with no code when `## Linter` says none and the user has not chosen to go on. It does not ask to run `$crav1-refresh-system-notes`. One task: it does not ask to run `$crav1-refresh-system-notes`.
flow:
- the one-task ending is a Run next entry, label above command, no `Next:` line.
- when the build walk or the range or all branch passes `approvals: already-done`, the one-task branch does not open `tool-approvals.md`.
- the held check never refuses a task claimed by you.
- `walk_progress.py readiness --vendor codex` reads you from `--user` or `git config user.name`; your claimed task's gate has `refused` false and `reason` `in progress by you`.
- when `--recommend` prints a `checkout:` line, the task-line branch is only on origin or is the head of an open pull request.
- The build checks it out (`git checkout <name>` makes the local tracking branch) without the branch card.
- when `$crav1-build-walk` opened this skill, do not print the open-pr Next.
- when a named person's yes is not on record, the parent writes or offers an `## Approval needed` item.
- It does not write `Approved:`.
- A matching `Approved:` line means that yes is on record.
- A live `apply` still needs the user's own yes in that run, and the task stays unticked until `check` is ok.
- on a base branch the Build prompt has no Stay, a headless run stops unless `new-branch`, a task naming a base branch is blocked, and the worker returns blocked on a base before any edit or commit.
- **`$crav1-build-tasks`** opens with one question: which tasks to build, one `T#`, a range, or all unticked, listing the ready ones with the `$crav1-tasks-ready-to-build` rules.
- Every task runs in its own worker (implement, commit, verify, optional fix), and every path ends by naming `$crav1-open-pr`.
- Inside each worker (was `$crav1-implement-task`): One `tasks.md` row, then run its verify step.
- Inside each worker (was `$crav1-implement-task`): Before the tests, checks the local dependencies they need (Azurite, a database container, an emulator) and asks start, skip, or stop for one that is not running.
- One task (was `$crav1-complete-task`): Isolated worker for one `T#`: implement → commit → verify → optional fix; persist commit style as a rule.
- One task (was `$crav1-complete-task`): When a local test dependency is not running, the worker returns `needs_dependency` with a `BLOCKER:` line, and you answer start, skip, or stop.
- A range or all (was `$crav1-complete-tasks`): Orchestrates one worker per `T#` (`T1-T3` or all unchecked); stops the batch when a worker needs you.
- a task's `(branch: …)` is offered first (Recommended) in the Build prompt; range and all-tasks runs switch to each task's branch on a clean tree, and a missing branch blocks that task.
- offers to create a missing task sub-branch from its spec branch and writes its `(into …)` marker after the yes.
- the branch question is its own card, before permissions, and a typed branch name on that card is the answer.
- A missing answer, or one that belongs on the other card, is re-asked.
- The offered branch is the build map row (`scripts/build_map.py --recommend T# --vendor codex`).
- A different pick writes `(map: <picked>)` and does not commit it.
- A missing person's yes is `needs_yes` and a Waiting line, not blocked, and the task stays unticked.
- A new `.sh` file with no `*.sh eol=lf` rule, when autocrlf is true or the host is Windows, offers `*.sh text eol=lf` and does not add it without a yes.
- the offered branch is the first line of `--recommend`.
- The card lists that option first and says where the name came from: the task line, the build map, or new.
- A `because:` line is the description when a name was skipped.
- when the ready check result is `ready` or `ready-partial`, the tasks in `can_start` may start.
- A held task (`refused`) is refused with its reason, including `held, waits on T#`.
- When the result is `not-ready`, no worker starts.
- a recorded-merged or already-verified row that is still `[ ]` is tick-only.
- `scripts/tick_only.py` ticks `[x]` and starts no worker when the result is `ready` or `ready-partial`, including when that task is already done for `can_start`.
- A `not-ready` result does not tick and does not start a worker.
- The spec folder is `scripts/resolve_spec.py`: exact folder first (`orders 1.0` matches `orders-1-0`), then one unique playbook basename, spec title, or work-item name.
- tick-only ticks a recorded-merged or already-verified `[ ]` row whatever the ready-check result, including `not-ready`.
- A `not-ready` result still starts no worker for any other task.
- `scripts/resolve_spec.py` then accepts one unique ordered token subsequence (`cc 1.0` matches `cc-process-1-0`).
- a live command the assistant's permission check refused, when the user's yes is already on record, is `permission_refused`, not `needs_yes`.
- `scripts/permission_block.py --vendor codex` distinguishes the two.
- the spec folder command is `<interpreter> -X utf8 <skill crav1-tasks-ready-to-build>/scripts/resolve_spec.py "<query>" --root docs/specs`.
- Tick-only is `scripts/tick_only.py --root <spec-folder> T#`.
- `--recommend` names `docs/specs/<slug>`.
- On Windows `<interpreter>` is `python` with `PYTHONUTF8=1`.
- Elsewhere it is `python3`.

## Choice words
- question: Which tasks
  - `one-task`: one task (add `T#`, or the first unticked)
  - `range`: a range (add `T#-T#`)
  - `all-tasks`: all unticked tasks
- question: Branch
  - `new-branch`: on a base or other branch, create feat/<slug> from the into branch
called_by: Called by the user and by `crav1-build-task-agent`.
runs by itself: Inside each worker: Calls `$crav1-create-feature-branch` before code. One task: Calls `$crav1-create-feature-branch` and `crav1-build-task-agent`. A range or all: Calls `$crav1-create-feature-branch` and `crav1-build-task-agent` once per `T#`.
you run next: $crav1-open-pr; $crav1-verify-build-against-spec; $crav1-finalize-commit
first: `$crav1-build-tasks @docs/specs/<slug>/`
walkthrough: from-plan-to-build.md
human: https://github.com/Crav1on/crav1-spec-kit/blob/v1.211.0/docs/reference/skills/crav1-build-tasks.md
